title: Twist-on wire connector, small (22 to 14 AWG, 2 to 3 conductors)

sources.citation: game-design, inside the general class of UL 486C-listed twist-on connectors (cited by number; the standard was not read): makers sell them in a few colour-coded sizes, each rated for a count range and a size range of copper conductors, stripped about 1/2 in. This fictional small size takes 2 to 3 copper conductors of 22 to 14 AWG, solid or stranded, not aluminium, with a combined size from 22 + 22 AWG (651068 µm²) to 14 + 14 AWG (4161820 µm², from the gauge table's areaUm2). The bounds are a paraphrased, simplified envelope chosen for play: no maker's combination chart was read or reproduced, so they are labelled game-design until one is read (ADR 0018 §4.4). The 13 ± 2 mm strip and 11 mm of twisted engagement are game-design too.

game-design (ADR 0018 §4.1, §11): R₀ = 0.5 mΩ for a twist-on joint, between the spring cage (0.3 mΩ) and the back-stab (1.0 mΩ), within NBS Building Science Series 128's (1980, read in the P3 pre-audit) 1.5 mΩ acceptance limit for an assembled connection. Every landed conductor gets it with a fixed spring force (r = 1), scaled only by strip length, nicks and the metal (ADR 0018 §4.4).

game-design (ADR 0018 §3.3; F3.6 reads them): the joint sits inside an insulating shell, so its heat path to the device (taken at ambient) is small, 0.01 W/K, against the screw class's 0.026 W/K; the clamp's heat capacity is a physics estimate, about 2 g of steel spring and the twisted copper ends × about 450 J/(kg·K), rounded to 1 J/K.
game-design: a 16 × 22 × 16 mm tapered shell with its one splice terminal at the open end, conductors entering along −y; not modelled on a product.
